knowledge_base.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
responses: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the broad field of building systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence. Machine learning is a branch of AI in which models learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions.
Machine learning is one way to build AI: a model is trained on examples, then uses the patterns it learned to handle new inputs. Deep learning is a subset that uses multi-layer neural networks.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: Python is a readable, general-purpose programming language used in automation, web development, data analysis, and AI. Start with variables, strings, numbers, conditionals, loops, functions, and collections such as lists and dictionaries.
A good way to learn Python is to write small programs and build up gradually. Functions package reusable logic, while lists and dictionaries help organize related data.

knowledge_base.title: Internet of Things
responses: The Internet of Things (IoT) connects physical devices that collect or exchange data. A sensor measures something in the environment, a network carries its data, and software can analyze it or trigger an action.
An IoT system commonly combines sensors, connected devices, communication networks, data processing, and an application. Security and privacy should be considered throughout the design.

knowledge_base.title: Cloud Computing
responses: Cloud computing provides computing resources—such as servers, storage, databases, and software—over a network on demand. IaaS offers infrastructure, PaaS provides a managed application platform, and SaaS delivers ready-to-use software.

The cloud lets organizations provision shared computing resources without owning every physical server. Common benefits include flexible scaling and usage-based pricing; availability, security, and cost still need active management.

knowledge_base.title: Data Science
responses: Data science uses programming, statistics, and subject knowledge to turn data into useful insights. A typical workflow is to define a question, collect and clean data, explore it, analyze or model it, and communicate the results.
Data analysis starts by asking a clear question and checking data quality. Visualization can reveal patterns, while statistical methods help assess whether an apparent pattern is meaningful.

knowledge_base.title: Cybersecurity
responses: Cybersecurity protects systems, networks, and information from unauthorized access or disruption. Useful foundations include strong unique passwords, multi-factor authentication, software updates, careful handling of links, and regular backups.
A useful security model considers confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Reduce risk with layered protections such as access controls, encryption, updates, monitoring, and user awareness.

knowledge_base.title: Networking
responses: Computer networking connects devices so they can exchange data. Protocols define how communication works; for example, IP addresses help route traffic, DNS maps domain names to addresses, and TCP provides reliable data delivery.
A network is a group of connected devices and the rules they use to communicate. Routers forward traffic between networks, while switches connect devices within a local network.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of steps for solving a problem or completing a task. A recipe is a familiar everyday example.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: A variable is a named reference to a value that a program can use or change. In Python, for example, `score = 10` assigns the value 10 to score.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: A data type describes what kind of value a program is using. Common Python types include integers, floating-point numbers, strings, and Booleans.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: A conditional lets a program choose which instructions to run based on a test. Python uses `if`, `elif`, and `else` for these decisions.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: A loop repeats instructions. A `for` loop commonly processes items in a collection, while a `while` loop repeats as long as its condition remains true.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: A function is a reusable block of code that can accept inputs (parameters) and optionally return a result. Functions help organize programs into manageable pieces.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: A Python list is an ordered, changeable collection, written with square brackets, such as `[1, 2, 3]`. Lists can hold multiple values.

knowledge_base.title: Python
responses: A Python dictionary stores values under unique keys, for example `{'name': 'Asha'}`. It is useful when each value has a meaningful label.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing problems in a program. Reproduce the issue, read error messages, inspect relevant values, and change one thing at a time.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: Version control records changes to files over time. Git is a widely used tool that lets people review history, create branches, and collaborate on code.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: An API is a defined way for software components to communicate. A web API often lets one application request or update data through HTTP.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: A database stores and organizes information so it can be retrieved or updated. Relational databases use tables, and SQL is a common language for working with them.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: An operating system manages a computer's hardware and provides services for applications. Windows, macOS, and Linux are examples.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: Web development builds websites and web applications. HTML structures content, CSS styles it, and JavaScript adds interactive behavior in the browser.

knowledge_base.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
responses: In machine learning, a model learns patterns from examples called training data. Its performance should be checked on data it did not train on.

knowledge_base.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
responses: Supervised learning trains a model using examples that include the correct target answer, such as labeled images. The model learns to predict targets for new inputs.

knowledge_base.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
responses: Unsupervised learning looks for structure in data without supplied target labels. Clustering is one example: it groups similar data points.

knowledge_base.title: Cloud Computing
responses: Software as a Service (SaaS) is software delivered over a network, commonly through a browser. The provider manages the underlying application infrastructure.

knowledge_base.title: Cybersecurity
responses: Phishing is a deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or opening something harmful. Verify the sender and destination before clicking, and report suspicious messages.

knowledge_base.title: Cybersecurity
responses: Use long, unique passwords for each account, store them in a reputable password manager, and enable multi-factor authentication when available.

knowledge_base.title: Study Skills
responses: A practical study plan sets a small goal, schedules regular practice, and includes a project to apply each new idea. Review what you learned and adjust the next goal based on what felt difficult.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: Start programming with one beginner-friendly language such as Python. Learn variables, conditionals, loops, and functions, then build small projects and practice reading error messages.

knowledge_base.title: IBM SkillsBuild
responses: IBM SkillsBuild offers learning resources, but course availability, certificates, and eligibility can change. Check the official IBM SkillsBuild website for current program details: skillsbuild.org.

knowledge_base.title: Programming Foundations
responses: Programming means writing instructions that a computer can execute. Programs combine data, decisions, repetition, and reusable operations to solve problems.
